items.title: (a) String Plucked at its Middle Point

source_refs.note: (a) String Plucked at its Middle Point: a main subheading of 7.5 Stationary waves on a stretched string, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 147-147.

blocks.text: If the string is plucked at its middle point, two transverse waves will originate from this point. One of them will move towards the left end of the string and the other towards the right end. When these waves reach the two clamped ends, they are reflected back thus giving rise to stationary waves. As the two ends of the string are clamped, no motion will take place there. So, nodes will be formed at the two ends and one mode of vibration of the string will be as shown in Fig. 7.7(a) with the two ends as nodes with one antinode in between. Visually, the string seems to vibrate in one loop.
